problems.title: Hajos-coordinate and stable-permutation qualifications
problems.decisive_evidence: The coordinate-swap of H=[[2,0],[1,2]] contains (1,2), whose first nonzero coordinate is odd. For H'=[[2,0,0],[0,2,0],[0,1,2]], simultaneous row/column transposition1,3 produces [[2,1,0],[0,2,0],[0,0,2]], not lower triangular.
problems.impact: The printed parity claim and the stated permutation operation fail in the unrestricted coordinates.
problems.repair_boundary: Choose Hajos coordinates; move the pure column index last while preserving other indices' order. After a needed sign change reduce last row modulo2 using column operations.
problems.counterevidence: The stable move preserves lower triangularity and establishes the intended Lemma2.6; the existence theorem is not refuted.
problems.discovery_attribution: Principal raised; native lattice helper independently checked the explicit examples and supplied the rank3 display.

problems.title: Loop and bridge qualifications in graph decompositions
problems.decisive_evidence: A single-loop graph has Flow=<1> and no loopless induced block, so the all-blocks condition in Theorem4.4 is vacuous but the flow is not a rank1 tiling lattice. A single ordinary edge has nonzero Cut=Z despite its block being declared trivial. Triangle plus loop has Flow=<3>+Z with the same d-invariant as <3>, but <3> cannot stabilize the larger rank flow.
problems.impact: Unrestricted auxiliary graph statements and the algorithm need explicit loop/bridge handling. The Proposition3.8 example is conditional on the usual bridge-free meaning of 2-edge-connected allowing loops.
problems.repair_boundary: Use loopless graphs or retain/reject loop blocks and account for Z loop factors; include bridge blocks for cuts. Lemma4.3 needs vertex-sum direct sum, not unwarranted two-connectedness.
problems.counterevidence: Reduced Tait graphs are loopless and bridgeless; a tiling flow lattice excludes norm1 loops. The intended main link classification is not refuted.
problems.discovery_attribution: Principal raised graph boundary tests; native lattice helper confirmed and traced the loop example into literal Theorem4.4.

problems.title: Simple cut-lattice vectors need not be one directed bipartition cut
problems.decisive_evidence: On C4 orient two paths v0->v1->v2 and v0->v3->v2. Potential z=(2,1,0,1) gives gradient (1,1,1,1) in Cut and is simple since each integral summand product a(1-a)<=0. A middle vertex would have to lie both inside and outside a single directed-cut partition.
problems.impact: The claimed equivalence of definitions is false even for a loopless two-connected graph. Subsequent statements must specify the broad cut-lattice meaning.
problems.repair_boundary: Use a simple cut-space vector, equivalently a compatible edge-disjoint union of directed cuts. Orthogonality proves reversing it in an acyclic orientation remains acyclic.
problems.counterevidence: For a directed cycle after reversal, pairing with the cut is minus the count of reversed edges and must vanish; hence the same cycle already existed. Unique-short-characteristic proof survives.
problems.discovery_attribution: Principal constructed C4 test; native lattice helper independently confirmed and recorded repair.

independent_acceptance_scope.result: All five existing problem groups are supported in the primary AAM. The graph counterexamples retain their loop/bridge and terminology limits; the positive-definite sign error is decisive, while the checked core Floer applications actually use sharp equalities. The unresolved diagram-identification step is not promoted to a confirmed error.
counterevidence_and_severity_basis: P1 concerns chosen coordinates and a faulty permutation operation; the stable permutation establishes the same basis-existence statement.

P2 affects unrestricted auxiliary graph statements; reduced Tait graphs in the core application are explicitly loopless and bridgeless. The Proposition3.8 test remains conditional on the usual edge-deletion meaning allowing loops.
P3 is an incompatible equivalence of cut definitions; the broad cut-lattice definition is already present, and orthogonality preserves the acyclicity argument actually needed downstream.
P4's false converse concerns reducedness detection by flow stabilization; bridge-type curls remain allowed by the normalized-determinant statement.
P5 is Minor because Theorem6.1, Lemma6.3 and the checked cubiquity chain use sharp equality, not the reversed inequality. This is actual dependency evidence, not a repair-length argument.
